claims.nodeLabel: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
claims.text: The originator-prefixed numbering (DOW-, ODNI-, FBI-) indicates the tranches were assembled by pulling from multiple agencies' holdings under a single presidential tasking rather than compiled from one department's files. Reasoning: a single-department dump would not need agency prefixes, and ODNI-UAP-D001 is an ODNI-originated document published in a DoW release series.

a.label: AARO FY2024 Consolidated Annual Report on UAP

edges.label: 'Lack of timely and actionable sensor data' against 51 released sensor videos
edges.note: The FY2024 report attributes AARO's analytic constraint to sensor-data scarcity nineteen months before the same department published 51 sensor videos in a single tranche, all of incidents predating the report.

edges.label: letter said to be answered by the tranche
edges.note: Release 02 is the only tranche with an identified congressional trigger - Luna's April 2026 letter - and the letter itself has not been published.

edges.label: Hearing, then letter, then release - the causal spine of 2026
edges.note: The sequence runs from sworn testimony that video was being withheld, through a subcommittee chair's letter to the Secretary, to a release channel that bypassed the office entirely.

edges.note: 64 files including 51 sensor videos in a DOW-UAP-PR050 to PR099 series; the 5.6GB video bundle is the largest of the five.

edges.label: Third tranche, 12 June 2026
edges.note: 72 files with the FBI the largest contributor at 29 files, including a less-redacted CIA Robertson Panel record.

a.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters

edges.label: Fourth tranche, 10 July 2026
edges.note: 227MB of documents and 1.4GB of video spanning the 1940s to 2026, published without any stated file count.

b.label: FBI Records: The Vault - UFO collection

edges.label: Published FBI 62-HQ-83894, well beyond the Vault's 1947-1954 scope
edges.note: The Bureau's master flying disc file covering 1947 to 1968 was released as a single 101MB PDF through war.gov rather than through the FBI's own reading room.

edges.label: Released Apollo 12 and Apollo 17 mission records
edges.note: Apollo mission records including cockpit transcript describing 'very bright particles or fragments' appear in the first tranche.

b.label: ODNI-UAP-D001 - serving senior intelligence officer's UAP encounter narrative

edges.label: Published the serving officer's encounter narrative
edges.note: A serving senior intelligence officer's first-person narrative of a one-hour, multi-witness encounter, published under an ODNI document number five months after the event.

b.label: CIA FOIA Reading Room - UFO collection

edges.label: Released a less-redacted 1953 Robertson Panel record
edges.note: A version of the Agency's own foundational UAP document less redacted than the one in its public reading room appeared seventy-three years later, by executive direction.

b.label: FBI Records: The Vault - UFO collection

edges.label: 29 FBI files including a 2021-2025 orb corpus and an agents' own FD-1057
edges.note: The tranche established the FBI as an active modern UAP collector, a posture invisible in its own Vault collection last modified in 2013.

edges.label: Released NASA Gemini-era crew debriefings
edges.note: Gemini crew debriefings and 1962 Cronkite-Cooper interview audio were published in the third tranche.

edges.label: Assessment language reappears despite the no-comment posture
edges.note: Release 04 material was characterised as consistent with balloons or sensor artefacts and as not clear evidence of unknown aircraft, reverting to the AARO idiom the release programme had disclaimed.

b.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters

edges.label: ODNI coordinating authority for the release programme
edges.note: Gabbard described the first release as an ongoing joint effort between intelligence and defence agencies; ODNI-numbered documents appear inside the war.gov series.

edges.label: By the fourth tranche the programme stopped stating what it released
edges.note: Releases 01, 02, 03 and 05 have published file counts; Release 04 has none on the portal or in independent inventories.
